fix_verdicts.evidence: ProxyTlsCloseTest no longer reads SSLSocket.isClosed() as its proof. RecordingSslSockets wraps every SSLSocket in RecordingSocket (ProxyTlsCloseTest.java:540-560), which records each close() call with its thread and plain.isClosed() before delegating. assertAllClosed (361-374) requires a recorded close() per created SSLSocket, each after the plain close. The cross-thread abort test (286-323) also asserts zero closes before the abort and no close on the res.abort thread. I re-ran mutant B myself (Proxy.releaseOnAbort listener calls exchange.release() instead of releaseOnAbortThread()): 9 tests, 1 failed, sec_PROXY_005_anAbortOnAnotherThreadClosesTheSslSocketWithoutWaitingForTheReader with 'the SSLSocket's close() ran on the thread that called res.abort, Time-limited test, while the request thread could still be reading it'. The mutant was reverted and git diff matched r4-before.diff byte for byte (cmp). The fixer's mutant A (closeConnection without the SSLSocket close) is also killed by the recorded-close assertion by construction, since no close() is recorded at all. The assertion is no longer vacuous.

ProxyExchange.release(boolean) (205-231) keeps the exactly-once CAS. It cancels the reservation, then closes, then runs limiter.release in nested finallys. releaseOnAbortThread() = release(false) closes only the recorded plain socket. BackendClient.connect records it with exchange.plainSocket before every connect (BackendClient.java:77-80), so the fallback to the attached SSLSocket cannot occur on the abort path. The listener registered in Proxy.releaseOnAbort is the only caller. Every path from res.relay on still closes the SSLSocket, checked against DefaultResponse, the only Response implementation in main code (no wrapper found). (a) An abort with no copy running: abort() calls closeInput when !copyRunning, before the listeners (DefaultResponse:851-871). (b) An abort during the copy: runTransfer's finally runs closeInput on the copy thread (775). (c) An abort before relay: startBody's refusal runs closeQuietly(in) (688-691). (d) Response.relay default closes in. RelayedBodyStream.close runs super.close (SocketBodyStream.close -> BackendClient.closeConnection) whatever the released flag. Exactly-once holds: after releaseOnAbortThread, RelayedBodyStream.close's release() is a no-op but the SSLSocket close still runs. A new mutant, M3 (release(false) skips limiter.release), failed 7 of 663 proxy tests, so the slot return on the abort path is pinned by tests. It was reverted and verified by cmp. API 21: animalsnifferMain --rerun passed. Residual (unchanged, out of scope): on Conscrypt the wakeup of a blocked SSL_read now relies only on the plain-socket close (Android IoBridge.closeAndSignalBlockedThreads / the close monitor in Conscrypt's sslSelect). It is not device-verified.

new_findings.claim: Three round-3 javadocs list the threads that close the SSLSocket, and the list is incomplete. ProxyExchange.release (178-181): 'Its callers run on the thread that owns the connection ... the forward path ..., and the relayed body's close'. ProxyExchange.releaseOnAbortThread (193-194): 'The SSLSocket is closed by the thread that owns the relayed body, after its read returned'. BackendClient.closeConnection (~133-135): 'It runs only on ... the request thread, or the thread that owns the relayed body once its read returned'. In path (a), an abort while no copy runs, DefaultResponse.abort calls closeInput on the aborting thread. That is the adapter thread of abortByExchange or any res.abort caller, before the listeners run. So RelayedBodyStream.close -> release() -> BackendClient.closeConnection, and the SSLSocket close, run there and not on a thread that 'owns the relayed body after its read returned'. The safety property the docs rely on, that no read of the connection is under way, still holds: copying is set and read under the response lock, so no reader exists when copyRunning is false. Only the thread description is wrong.
new_findings.evidence: DefaultResponse.java:851-871 (abort: copyRunning = copying under lock; if (!copyRunning) closeInput(); then abortListeners.abort()). sec_PROXY_005_anAbortBeforeTheCopyStartsClosesTheSslSocket exercises this path: the close comes from res.abort's caller.
new_findings.proposed_fix: Reword the three javadocs to state the real invariant: the SSLSocket is closed only by a thread under which no read of the connection is under way. That is the request thread before res.relay, the copy thread after its read returned, or the aborting thread when no copy is running (the response closes the relayed input itself then). The res.onAbort listener, which may run during a read, closes only the plain socket.

new_findings.claim: The test class javadoc contradicts itself. Lines 48-49 say the three proxy-side closes 'each close the plain socket under TLS, never the SSLSocket'. Lines 52-54 say 'Every path also closes the SSLSocket itself once the plain socket under it is closed', and assertAllClosed asserts a close() call on every SSLSocket. The first sentence is left over from before R2-001 and is now false.
new_findings.proposed_fix: Change 'close the plain socket under TLS, never the SSLSocket, whose TLS 1.3 duplex close ...' to 'close the plain socket under TLS first, never starting with the SSLSocket, whose TLS 1.3 duplex close ...'.
